subskill: Evaluate Function at a Given Value
prompt:
$$f(x) = 4(g(x)) - 3$$

$$g(x) = |11x - 7|$$

The functions $f$ and $g$ are defined by the given equations. What is the value of $f(-12)$?
explanation: Choice A is correct. To find the value of $f(-12)$, first evaluate the inner function $g(-12)$. Substituting $x = -12$ into $g(x) = |11x - 7|$ gives $g(-12) = |11(-12) - 7|$. Calculating inside the absolute value: $11(-12) = -132$, and $-132 - 7 = -139$. Applying the absolute value gives $g(-12) = |-139| = 139$. Now substitute this result into the outer function: $f(-12) = 4(g(-12)) - 3 = 4(139) - 3$. Multiplying gives $4(139) = 556$, and subtracting $3$ gives $556 - 3 = 553$. Therefore, $f(-12) = 553$.
